title: Handoff Heuristics Labbook
content:
Purpose: scratchpad for investigating odd handoff behavior when regional capacity is constrained. Not a formal postmortem yet — keeping a low-fidelity timeline, commands tried, and hypotheses to iterate with SREs and runtime folks.

Summary of symptom (observed 2026-03-09 18:40 UTC):
- Upstream: traffic to region us-west-2 started seeing an elevated 502/503 rate from the router layer (~2.8% for a ten-minute window).
- Downstream: many requests routed to fallback region us-east-1, but some requests were dropped during egress handoff (client saw truncated streaming responses, no final "done" token).
- Affected workloads: mostly chat flows with long context (seq len > 2048) and models that rely on KV-cache reuse.
- Edge clue: traces show router accepted request, created an outbound connection to serving host, then connection teardown with ECONNRESET immediately after first ChunkedData event.

Quick repro attempt (local curl + streaming):
- curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-7b-lf", "input":"<long conversation>"}' \
  https://api.redwood.test/v1/stream
  -> repeated truncated output after 4–8 tokens.

Live checks run from SRE jumpbox (us-west-2):
- kubectl -n serving logs -l app=router --since=15m | grep "egress-handshake"
- tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/handoff.pcap 'host 10.1.23.45 and port 443' (nothing obvious at packet layer besides RST from the serving host IP)
- curl -I https://serving-01.us-west-2.internal:8443/health -> 200

Command snippets and outputs (sanitized):
- grpcurl -plaintext serving-01.us-west-2.internal:8080 rwd.Service.GetModelStatus
  -> {"model":"rwd-7b-lf","kv_cache":"enabled","seq_max":4096,"mem_available_gb":23}

- kubectl exec -it router-7f9 -- /bin/sh -c "cat /proc/net/tcp | grep 01:ABCD" -> showed multiple TIME_WAIT sockets to the same serving host.

- router debug logs (excerpt):
  [2026-03-09T18:39:42Z] route=us-west-2 target=serving-01 conn=establish ok
  [2026-03-09T18:39:43Z] route=us-west-2 target=serving-01 egress-handshake error=peer_reset frame=0
  [2026-03-09T18:39:43Z] route=us-west-2 fallback-policy=region-redirect chose=us-east-1 reason=egress-failed

Hypotheses (ranked, quick):
1) Serving host evicts or resets long-lived connections when KV-cache pressure is high — first-chunk causes memory spike and process OOM-protection triggers per-connection RST. Evidence: mem_available reported 23GB but per-process RSS spikes on large contexts in metrics.
2) Router TCP keepalive/half-close mismatch: router initiates TLS shutdown and then re-uses same socket for fallback race, leading to corrupted stream. Evidence: TIME_WAIT / RST clusters and truncated chunked responses.
3) Middlebox (NAT/gw) imposes connection rate limits during surge and silently drops longer upstream streams. Evidence: not yet strong; packet captures don't show ICMP blackhole but do show short gaps.
4) A bug in our streaming codec where an early "done" frame is suppressed when handoff occurs mid-stream. Evidence: stack traces not captured yet.

Notes on fallback policy and handoff flow (design assumptions):
- When egress fails, router consults fallback-policy for request: (a) regional-redirect, (b) degrade-to-embedding-only, (c) model-variant-fallback.
- For streaming, we must either: finish active stream then attempt fallback OR preemptively re-establish a fallback stream and stitch payloads. Our current strategy attempts to stitch which is implemented in router v2.1.2.

Quick local test to force deterministic handoff: simulate egress-reset after N tokens using the test harness:
- python tests/stream_harness.py --target serving-01 --kill-after-tokens 5 --seed 42
  Observed: harness forced RST and router attempted fallback, but fallback stream returned duplicates of first 5 tokens and then hung (no final end-of-stream).

Relevant config snippets (current prod-ish):
- router-config.yaml (excerpt):
  fallback-policy: regional-redirect
  streaming-stitch: true
  stitch-timeout-ms: 500
  max-concurrent-handshakes: 64
  connection-reuse: true

Open questions / checks to run:
- Check per-process oom_kill logs on serving node around 18:39 UTC (dmesg, /var/log/kern.log).
- Dump router runtime stacks for v2.1.2 during repro to check codec state machine and whether it emits final frames when stream aborted mid-stitch. (gdb + sigquit pattern).
- Confirm whether stitch-timeout-ms=500 is too aggressive — maybe stitches get partial bytes. Try increasing to 2000ms in a canary router group.
- Validate whether connection-reuse=true causes corruption when TLS session is closed and re-opened by middlebox. Consider toggling to false in a canary.

Action plan (immediate):
- 1) Ask SRE to snapshot serving-01 process metrics and histograms (RSS, page faults) for 18:30–18:45; collect /proc/<pid>/maps and pprof if feasible. (Assigned: Marco)
- 2) Deploy a router canary with stitch-timeout-ms=2000 and connection-reuse=false to a small subset of traffic (5%): monitor truncation rate over next 60 minutes. (Assigned: Riley)
- 3) Add temporary increased logging for streaming stitch state machine (trace level) and roll for 30 minutes. (Assigned: me)
- 4) Re-run the python harness with --save-pcap and --save-router-trace to have artifacts for offline debugging.

Notes-to-self:
- If canary reduces truncations but increases tail latency, we may need an adaptive stitch-timeout that correlates to measured RTT to serving host.
- Consider fallback policy change for long-context requests: prefer model-variant-fallback (quantized variant in same region) rather than cross-region redirect. Cross-region increases RTT and surface area for mid-handshake failures.
- Patch idea: when stitching streams, include a small sequence checksum in frames so router can detect duplication/missing frames when stitching from two distinct connections. Low-risk and helps detect corruption.

Logs and snippets to attach to ticket (collected):
- /var/log/router/router.2026-03-09.trace.gz (grep egress-handshake)
- /tmp/handoff.pcap
- tests/run_2026-03-09_harness.log

Hypothesis test matrix (brief):
- A: Increase stitch-timeout -> expected: fewer truncations, maybe added latency.
- B: Disable connection reuse -> expected: fewer RST/TIME_WAIT reuse artifacts.
- C: Force fallback to model-variant in-region -> expected: reduced cross-region failures; isolates whether issue is transit vs serving host.
- D: Reproduce with identical long-context but single-token streaming (non-stitch) to see if stitch logic specifically causes truncation.

Unresolved / follow-ups:
- Need to correlate router OpenTelemetry traces with serving host logs (trace IDs) — ask infra to turn on 1s retention for traces matching sample trace_id.
- If root cause is serving OOM, need evaluation of per-request memory accounting + backpressure to router.

Random debugging notes and heuristics (for later):
- When replicating truncated-stream locally, stepping through our codec in the test harness showed that a "DONE frame" is emitted but the router's stitcher didn't forward it because it was waiting for a resume token from fallback stream. That indicates a race (stitch state machine not tolerant to early done).
- Consider adding a short-circuit: if primary emits DONE and fallback not yet started or hasn't sent resume token within N ms, forward DONE to client and mark request as complete. Safer for user experience than hanging.

Next sync: pull together first-pass artifacts and schedule 30-min session with SRE + serving owners tomorrow 2026-03-13 10:00 PT.

-- Aisha
